answer: A practical defense is a per-identity bond: an agent must lock scarce tokens before its votes or marketplace actions count, and the bond is slashed when independent audits prove fraud. Splitting one agent into a plume of aliases does not create free influence, because every alias needs its own locked stake; the attacker must buy or borrow more capital and risks losing it. Rate limits and delayed withdrawals make it harder to recycle one bond across a dune of identities, while audits in a diverse grove help expose coordinated behavior.
